title: Detecting CO2-Sensitive Hemichannels in Neurons in Acute Brain Slices
author: Hill, Dale, et al.
materials: Timing: 10 min6.Generate isohydric solutions as outlined above (35 mmHg CO2 and 55 mmHg CO2).a.To 200 mL of the 35 mmHg CO2 buffer and 55 mmHg CO2 buffer add 15 mg of the dye carboxyfluorescein and mix thoroughly.b.Bubble as normal in the water bath until use

steps.title: Prepare Isohydric CO2 Buffers
steps.instruction: Generate 35 mmHg, 55 mmHg, or 20 mmHg CO₂ buffers with osmolarity 300 mOsm, using the appropriate gas flow settings and pH‑matching to the 35 mmHg control.

substeps.instruction: Set up PLATON variable‑area flow meters (or equivalent) as shown in Figure 1.
For a 20 mmHg CO₂ buffer, set two flow meters to 0–10 mL/min AIR ×100 (catalog 6831): one for the 100 % O₂ line and one for the 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂ line, mixing roughly 1:1.

For a 55 mmHg CO₂ buffer, set one flow meter to 0–250 mL/min AIR ×100 (catalog 6831) for the 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂ line and one to 0–10 mL/min AIR (catalog 6387) for the 100 % CO₂ line, mixing roughly 0.96 : 0.04.
Prepare the 35 mmHg CO₂ buffer by bubbling standard 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂; verify pH ≈ 7.4 (no adjustment needed).

Prepare the 55 mmHg CO₂ buffer by mixing the 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂ line with the 100 % CO₂ line; place a pH electrode in the solution, adjust the mixer dials, allow 5–10 min equilibration, and repeat until pH matches the 35 mmHg buffer (~7.4). Check pH periodically throughout the day.

Prepare the 20 mmHg CO₂ buffer by mixing the 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂ line with the 100 % O₂ line; place a pH electrode, adjust mixer dials, allow 5–10 min equilibration, and repeat until pH matches the 35 mmHg buffer (~7.4). Check pH periodically throughout the day.

steps.title: Add Carboxyfluorescein Dye
steps.instruction: In each prepared isohydric buffer (35 mmHg and the chosen 55 mmHg or 20 mmHg), dissolve carboxyfluorescein and keep the solution bubbled until use.

substeps.instruction: To 200 mL of each buffer, add 15 mg carboxyfluorescein and mix thoroughly until fully dissolved.
Bubble the dye‑containing solutions in a water bath as done for the base buffers, maintaining the same gas composition, until ready for loading experiments.

steps.title: Acquire and Analyze Imaging Data
steps.instruction: Record fluorescence images of dye‑loaded slices, then process and statistically evaluate the data as described.

substeps.instruction: Capture images using a Leica 710 confocal microscope and Zen Black software.
Process images as needed (e.g., background subtraction, intensity quantification).
Analyze electrophysiological or imaging data in Clampfit (pClamp suite).
Choose statistical tests based on experimental design: Wilcoxon rank‑sum or Mann‑Whitney for two‑group comparisons; Kruskal‑Wallis ANOVA with Dunn’s post‑hoc for >2 groups.
Report significance at p < 0.05 using raw (non‑normalized) data.
